scope.flow: unregisterVault() in WERC7575ShareToken.sol rejects vault removal when vault asset or share balances are non-zero

statements.text: A vault is registered in the WERC7575ShareToken vault registry such that unregisterVault() can be invoked for it
unregisterVault() requires both IERC7575Vault(vaultAddress).totalAssets() and ERC20(asset).balanceOf(vaultAddress) to be zero before allowing removal
Anyone can send even 1 wei of the asset directly to the vault, making ERC20(asset).balanceOf(vaultAddress) non-zero
The vault may lack a withdrawal or sweep mechanism to clear the donated asset balance
Attacker donates 1 wei of the asset directly to the vault address
Protocol governance calls unregisterVault() to remove the vault
unregisterVault() assumes any non-zero vault asset balance represents user liabilities, so a donated balance causes the removal guard to always revert
unregisterVault() always reverts while vaultBalance is non-zero, blocking vault removal
Vault lifecycle operations are prevented, including removing deprecated or faulty vaults, migrating users to a new vault implementation, and cleaning up stale vault registry entries
unregisterVault() should permit removal according to its intended guard, not be permanently blocked by a third-party dust donation that is not a user liability
The vault registry and unregisterVault() logic as described in the report match the deployed WERC7575ShareToken.sol behavior

ambiguities: No prior state is established showing an actual registered vault existed and governance invoked unregisterVault() in a real transaction; the scenario may be conditional.
No explicit statement identifies the actor who calls unregisterVault(); caller authorization is not specified.
Whether the deployed vault actually lacks a sweep mechanism is stated as a possibility ('may not'), not a confirmed fact.
No concrete transaction or incident demonstrates success of the griefing in practice.
